title: "Workshops"

The BGM Lab teaches workshops on Bayesian analysis of graphical models: at the Psychosystems Network Analysis summer and winter schools (PSYNETS) at the University of Amsterdam, at conferences, and at other summer schools. A workshop usually has three parts: a lecture on the ideas behind Bayesian network analysis, a hands-on tutorial in R and JASP, and an assignment with solutions.

::: {.placeholder}
What kinds of workshops do we offer (length, level, format), and who should people contact to invite us?
:::

## Learn the software

- The [bgms documentation](https://bayesian-graphical-modelling-lab.github.io/bgms/) has a [getting-started guide](https://bayesian-graphical-modelling-lab.github.io/bgms/guide/getting-started.html) and [worked analyses](https://bayesian-graphical-modelling-lab.github.io/bgms/examples/index.html) that take you from fitting a model to reporting the results.
- [easybgm](https://cran.r-project.org/package=easybgm) wraps the analysis in a few function calls; [JASP](https://jasp-stats.org) does it point-and-click. See [Software](software.qmd) for all our packages.

## Past workshops

Slides, R scripts, data, and exercises are in our [workshop repository](https://github.com/Bayesian-Graphical-Modelling-Lab/BGM_Workshops) on GitHub. You are welcome to use them in your own teaching.
